events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Oh my stars and garters, what a positively magnificent entrance hall! Why, I feel like a debutante at the grandest ball in all of Georgia! Y'all are just the sweetest bunch of treasure hunters a girl could hope to meet. Now, if nobody minds, I'm just going to take a teeny tiny peek at this charming little guest book here — a lady always signs in, and who knows what previous visitors might have left behind!

Clara Bellingham is on the case! Now, everyone here looks perfectly delightful, but let's see — the guest book might have names, dates, maybe even a little riddle or clue tucked between the pages. The Diamond won't find itself, sugar.
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.

Dick Dastardly: Ah-HA! Doily Manor at last! The treasure is as good as MINE! Nobody — and I mean NOBODY — is going to beat the great Reginald Foxworth to the prize! Muttley, stop snickering and pay attention! Now then, what have we here... a guest book! Perhaps some fool has helpfully written down exactly where the treasure is hidden. People are SO obligingly stupid!

Peter Perfect: What a splendid estate! Dusty, yes, but one can see the grandeur beneath. Now then — a gentleman always announces his arrival properly. Let me inspect this guest book. If Clara has already signed, her entry may reveal which way she ventured. And THEN — then I shall find her, and she shall see that James Hartwell is a man of both manners AND action!

Look at all these simpletons, just standing around in the foyer like tourists! While THEY gawk at the dusty portraits, I shall be three steps ahead, finding clues and hatching my BRILLIANT scheme. The fake medal might come in handy — perhaps I can use it to distract Muttley while I slip away with the real prize. Dastardly — I mean, Foxworth — you magnificent scoundrel, you've done it again! Well, not YET, but it's only a matter of time!
Dick Dastardly examined the guest-book.

My heart is thundering like a cavalry charge. Clara could be anywhere in this manor — the library, the kitchen, some hidden parlour. I must be systematic. I must be thorough. I must be... impossibly impressive when she finally lays eyes on me. First things first — the guest book. Every great quest begins with proper reconnaissance.
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right lads, we've made it to Doily Manor! Bit of a fixer-upper, innit? Now listen — we're here for one reason and one reason only: we gotta find Miss Clara Bellingham and make sure nobody lays a finger on her. I don't like the look of this place, not one bit. That chandelier up there looks like it's hanging by a thread, and — oi, watch your step, Clyde nearly tripped on that rug! Let's have a butcher's at this guest book, see if Clara's signed in already.

Something about that Sneekly fella gives me the willies. Can't say what it is exactly — maybe it's the way he keeps looking around all shifty-like. The lads feel it too. But we ain't detectives, we're just... well, we're the Ant Hill Mob, and we look after our own. Clara's somewhere in this manor, and we're gonna find her before anything dodgy happens.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the guest-book.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Good evening, dear guests! Welcome, welcome to Doily Manor! I am Mr. Pemberton, the estate manager. So delighted you could all make it for tonight's little... treasure hunt. Please do make yourselves at home — though I would advise against touching the chandelier. It is, shall we say, temperamental. Now, if you'll excuse me, I must attend to a few arrangements deeper in the house. Do enjoy the guest book — previous visitors have left the most fascinating entries!

Ah, what a magnificent collection of unsuspecting buffoons! But where — WHERE — is Clara Bellingham? She is not among this gaggle of costumed competitors. She must already be prowling the manor's darker corridors, sniffing out MY treasure. Every moment I waste glad-handing these racing enthusiasts is a moment she draws closer to the prize. I must find her before she finds it. The library... yes, the library calls to me. Ancient books, hidden passages, and perhaps a certain meddlesome heiress who needs to meet with a most unfortunate accident. The game, as they say, is magnificently afoot!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the null.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, bless my heart, that guest book was just charmin'! Now then, sugar plums, I do believe a lady of refinement ought to visit the Library next — after all, every great mystery starts between the pages of a good book! And did I hear somethin' about an inscription on the mantelpiece? Why, that sounds like exactly the kind of delightful little puzzle that makes an adventure worth havin'! Y'all are welcome to join me, of course — the more the merrier!

That inscription on the stone mantelpiece is calling to me like a magnolia in bloom. If there's a riddle carved into this old mansion, Clara Bellingham is going to crack it wide open. The Diamond has to leave a trail, and riddles are breadcrumbs for the clever.
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.

Dick Dastardly: Well well well, nothing of interest in that tedious little book — just the scrawlings of LESSER minds! I suggest you all stay RIGHT HERE and examine this fascinating coat rack — I hear it's a priceless antique, worth FAR more than any so-called treasure! Yes yes, very valuable coat rack indeed! Meanwhile, I shall, ah... stretch my legs. Purely for my HEALTH, you understand. Nothing to see, carry on!

Heh heh heh! Send them chasing after a worthless coat rack while the GREAT Reginald Foxworth makes a beeline for the Library! That inscription on the mantelpiece could be the key to everything! And if anyone follows me — well, I'll simply tell them the inscription says 'treasure is in the Kitchen.' Dastardly, you GENIUS!
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: No sign of Clara in the guest book — she clearly doesn't waste time on formalities. A woman after my own heart! Well then, ladies and gentlemen, while you all squabble over dusty ledgers, I shall venture forth to the Library. A carved inscription on a mantelpiece, you say? That has 'vital clue' written all over it — sometimes literally! And if Clara Bellingham happens to be there... well, she'll find that James Hartwell is a man who arrives precisely when he is needed most!
My palms are sweating. What if Clara is in the Kitchen instead? No — no second-guessing. A man of action commits to his course. The Library. The inscription. And perhaps... destiny.
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, I do hope you are all finding the guest book illuminating! Such rich history in these pages. Now, if you will pardon me, I must dash to the library — there are some, ah, arrangements to finalize for the next stage of your treasure hunt. Candles to light, doors to unlock, that sort of thing. Estate manager duties, you understand! Do take your time here — no rush at all, no rush at ALL!

Ha-HA! Perfect — they're all squabbling over the guest book like pigeons fighting over breadcrumbs! None of them suspect a thing. Dear, sweet, oblivious fools. Now I slip away to the library — the LIBRARY! — where ancient secrets lurk behind leather-bound spines and where, if fortune favors the magnificently wicked, I shall find Clara Bellingham before she uncovers the treasure's location. And when I find her... oh, it won't be anything so crude as a simple confrontation. No, no, NO! Vincent Marsh deals in ELABORATE misfortune — a bookshelf that topples at just the wrong moment, a hidden trapdoor that opens beneath unsuspecting feet! The chandelier gambit served me well in my youth, but tonight calls for something with more... literary flair. To the library! Destiny — and delicious villainy — awaits!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right lads, listen up! Clara ain't here, which means she's somewhere deeper in this creepy old pile, and that means she could be in DANGER! Terrible, horrible, unspeakable danger! Did you see the way that Sneekly fella slithered off? Gave me the absolute heebie-jeebies, he did! I can't put me finger on it, but something about him is... well, it's... it's just NOT RIGHT, is what it is! Clyde, stop picking at the wallpaper! Dum-Dum, put that candlestick down! We're heading to the Library — if Clara's anywhere, she's where the books are. She's a refined lady, ain't she? Now MOVE IT, lads — and for the love of all that's holy, watch out for that loose floorboard by the — OI! Clyde! I JUST said watch the floorboard! Right, he's fine, he's fine, just a bit of a stumble. Let's GO!

I'm proper worried, I am. That Sneekly — or Pemberton or whatever he calls himself — there's something behind them beady eyes of his. The way he told us to 'enjoy the guest book' like he WANTED us distracted while he went off to do who-knows-what. And that chandelier! One good sneeze and the whole lot comes crashing down. This manor's a death trap, and our Clara's in it somewhere. We ain't clever, the lads and me. We ain't heroes neither. But we're LOYAL, and that counts for something. We just gotta find her before trouble does.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, would you look at that! A genuine riddle carved right into the stone — how perfectly thrilling! Now let me see here... 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, sugar, that's as clear as sweet tea on a summer day! It's a MAP! Cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish — all things you'd find drawn on a map! Oh, I do hope this opens somethin' marvelous. Dick Dastardly, honey, isn't this just the most excitin' thing? And Rock, Gravel — y'all are in for a treat!

A riddle guarding the path to the Doily Diamond, I just know it! Every good treasure hunt has clues, and this mansion is practically gift-wrapping them for me. Now let's see what happens when I give this mantelpiece the answer it's been waiting for!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Ah-HA! The Library — sanctuary of knowledge, cathedral of wisdom, and — good heavens, what a magnificent mantelpiece! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, that's elementary! The answer is a MAP! A map, ladies and gentlemen! Cities marked but no houses built, forests drawn but no trees growing, rivers traced but no fish swimming! And where there's a riddle about a map in a manor like this, there's surely a map to be FOUND! Perhaps one that leads to a certain treasure — or better yet, to a certain Miss Clara Bellingham! Stand back, everyone — James Hartwell is on the case!

Please let this be the right answer. Please let there be a dramatic reveal. And PLEASE let Clara somehow hear about this moment of brilliant deduction. A man solves one riddle on a mantelpiece and suddenly he's the hero of the evening — that's how these things work, isn't it?
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Well well WELL, if it isn't the lovely Penelope and the — ah — ROCK collection! I see you're all gawking at this mantelpiece like fish at a worm. Allow ME, the GREAT Reginald Foxworth, to save you the trouble — I've seen this riddle before in my EXTENSIVE travels! The answer is quite obviously 'a DESERT!' Cities buried in sand, petrified forests, dried-up riverbeds — it's ALL about the desert! Now if I were you, I'd rush off to find something sandy — perhaps the Kitchen has a sandbox? A sandbox full of TREASURE, no doubt! Run along now, chop chop!

Heh heh HEH! A desert — what utter NONSENSE! The real answer is a MAP, and once these gullible fools scamper off to find a sandbox, I shall solve this riddle and claim whatever prize it reveals! Medal number — well, FIRST medal, technically, but who's counting? The GREAT Reginald Foxworth is counting, that's who!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, welcome, welcome to the library, everyone! Such a splendid room, is it not? Now, I must just inspect this mantelpiece — the old master always insisted it be kept in pristine condition. Let me see here... 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, how delightful! The previous Lord Bellingham did so love his little puzzles. The answer, of course, would be... a MAP!

Ha-HA! Let them think old Pemberton is simply a doddering fool who blurts out answers without thinking! In TRUTH, I solve this riddle to advance MY position in the hunt. If it reveals a map — or a clue TO a map — I shall note its location and arrange for Clara Bellingham to meet with a most unfortunate accident before she can follow the same trail. Oh, the EXQUISITE irony — the estate manager, helpfully solving puzzles for the guests, while secretly plotting their doom! Vincent Marsh, you magnificent devil, you've STILL got it!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare! I answered that riddle — a MAP, obviously — and now I simply must see what happened! Did y'all hear a click? I thought I felt somethin' shift in the stonework! Oh, this is more excitin' than a debutante ball in Savannah! Let me take a closer look at this magnificent mantelpiece — there could be a secret compartment, a hidden lever, or even a clue to the Doily Diamond itself! Sneekly, sugar, you're the estate manager — has anyone ever solved that riddle before?

My heart is just flutterin' like a hummingbird! If that riddle points to a map, then somewhere in this old mansion there's a map that leads to the Diamond. I can feel it in my bones — Clara Bellingham is on the trail, and nothin' is gonna stop her!
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Blimey, what a room! Look at all them BOOKS, lads! Thousands of 'em! Right, Clara ain't here neither, which is VERY concerning. That's every room we've checked and no Clara! She could be anywhere in this enormous death trap of a manor! Dum-Dum, DON'T sit in that chair, it's covered in dust and you'll — too late. Right, he's sneezing now. Lovely. Clyde, help me check these bookshelves — maybe there's a secret passage or something. That's how it works in them mystery stories, innit? You pull a book and a wall opens up and there's Clara having tea behind it. And keep your eyes on that Sneekly fella, lads. I'm not saying he's UP to something, because I can't rightly say WHAT he'd be up to, but... well... don't he just give you the WILLIES? The way he scurried in here ahead of everyone to 'light candles' and 'unlock doors'? What doors? WHAT CANDLES? I don't see no freshly lit candles! Something's off, lads. Something's VERY off.

The lads and me, we ain't got a single braincell between us when it comes to mysteries and riddles. But we've got INSTINCTS, and every instinct I've got is screaming that this Sneekly character is bad news. I just wish I could work out WHY. It's like... you know when you smell something funny but you can't find where it's coming from? That's Sneekly, that is. A funny smell you can't locate. And Clara — oh, poor Clara — she's somewhere in this manor without us to accidentally protect her. We've got to find her before something terrible happens!
The Ant Hill Mob examined the bookshelves.

Peter Perfect: Now hold on just one moment, Dastardly — or should I say, 'Reginald!' A DESERT? Cities buried in sand? That's the most preposterous thing I've ever heard, and I once tried to jump a canyon in a motorcar! The answer is a MAP — Penelope had it right, and so did I! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees — those are features DRAWN on a map, not buried under sand! Now then — if the riddle guards a secret, then the secret should reveal itself to those who answer correctly. Let me take a closer look at this magnificent stonework... a hidden compartment, perhaps? A sliding panel? James Hartwell leaves no stone unturned — ESPECIALLY not a mantelpiece stone!

My heart is absolutely POUNDING. If there's a hidden map behind this mantelpiece and I'm the one to find it — oh, Clara will hear about this. She'll hear how James Hartwell solved the ancient riddle AND discovered the secret passage while everyone else was arguing about deserts. This is my moment. Please, PLEASE let there be something dramatic behind this stone.
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Yes yes, very CLEVER, Penelope — a map, how OBVIOUS! I was merely TESTING you all with my desert answer, and you passed! Barely! Now if you'll excuse me, I notice these bookshelves are in a DISGRACEFUL state of disarray — several volumes are UPSIDE DOWN! As a man of IMPECCABLE literary taste, I simply CANNOT abide such slovenliness! I shall tidy them up — purely out of CIVIC DUTY, you understand!

Heh heh HEH! 'Tidying the bookshelves' — what a MAGNIFICENT cover story! Those upside-down books are OBVIOUSLY a clue — pull the right one and a secret passage opens, or a hidden map falls out! And while everyone else stands around YAKKING about riddles, the GREAT Reginald Foxworth will have the treasure map in his pocket! MEDAL, here I come!

Penelope Pitstop: Why, the answer is as plain as peaches in July — it's a MAP, of course! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — that's a map, through and through! Now let me just give this gorgeous stonework a proper lady's touch... there's always a hidden catch in these old manors, and Clara Bellingham has nimble fingers and a nose for secrets! Oh Sneekly, darlin', you said the old Lord Bellingham loved his puzzles — I'll bet my best parasol there's somethin' hidden right here in this mantelpiece!

Every bone in my body is tinglin'! If Sneekly already fiddled with this mantelpiece and somethin' clicked, then there's a mechanism here. And if there's a map inside, it could be the key to everything. I just need to find the right spot to press or pull. Oh, this is simply divine!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, yes, Miss Pitstop! As a matter of fact, the late Lord Bellingham solved it himself — he was quite the cartographer in his day, you know. Always poring over maps and atlases. I believe he kept his finest collection right here in the library, in fact! Now, if you'll all excuse me for just a moment, I must check that these bookshelves haven't suffered any water damage — the roof above the library has been rather temperamental, and some of these volumes are quite irreplaceable. Estate manager duties, you understand!

Ha-HA! The FOOLS — every last one of them is fixated on that mantelpiece like moths to a flame! But VINCENT MARSH sees what they do not — those upside-down books are no accident! Someone — Lord Bellingham himself, no doubt — arranged them as a MECHANISM! A lever, a switch, a trigger hidden in plain sight among dusty leather spines! And while these bumbling treasure hunters fumble with carved stone, I shall quietly investigate the REAL secret of this library. Oh, the delicious IRONY — the estate manager, dutifully checking for water damage, while actually unlocking the path to untold riches! And once I have the map in my magnificently villainous hands... then it's time to arrange a little ACCIDENT for dear Clara Bellingham. Wherever she is hiding, Vincent Marsh will FIND her!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the bookshelves.

Peter Perfect: Nobody move! I felt something shift in this stonework when I examined it — there's definitely a mechanism here. The riddle said MAP, and a map is EXACTLY what we need to find Clara and the Doily Diamond! Now, if my years of experience with precision engineering have taught me anything, it's that a carved mantelpiece with a riddle is NEVER just decorative. There's a catch, a lever, a spring-loaded panel — and James Hartwell is going to find it! Stand back, everyone — especially YOU, Dastardly, stop manhandling those books! If this thing has a counterweight system, I don't want anyone shifting anything until I've located the release! Here goes nothing — or rather, here goes EVERYTHING!

Oh, my hands are trembling. If I pull this off — if I actually reveal a hidden map or a secret passage right here in front of everyone — the story will reach Clara before I do. 'Did you hear about James Hartwell? Solved the ancient riddle AND found the hidden mechanism!' She'll be utterly charmed. She HAS to be. Please, please, PLEASE let this be spectacular and not just a dusty brick that crumbles in my hand.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Well! These books are in PERFECT order now, thanks to MY efforts! You're all VERY welcome! Now, I overheard that estate manager fellow mention something about the Laboratory being EXTREMELY dangerous — full of poisonous gases and man-eating machinery! NOBODY should go in there! Absolutely FATAL! I myself shall brave it ONLY to put up a warning sign, because I am a SELFLESS and CIVIC-MINDED gentleman!

Heh heh HEH! Tell them the Laboratory is DEADLY and they'll all stay RIGHT here squabbling over that mantelpiece! Meanwhile, the GREAT Reginald Foxworth will have the Laboratory — and whatever secrets it holds — ALL to himself! I am a GENIUS! An absolute GENIUS! Now to sneak away before that meddlesome Peter Perfect notices...
Dick Dastardly walked into the laboratory.

The Ant Hill Mob: Ere, lads — LADS! Look at this! Half these books are upside down! Now I ain't what you'd call a LITERARY man, but I'm fairly certain that ain't how you shelve a book! Someone's done this on PURPOSE, and in my experience — limited as it is — when things are arranged funny in a creepy old manor, it means there's a SECRET PASSAGE or a hidden whatnot behind it! Dum-Dum, you great lump, you're already grabbing at that one — well go on then, PULL IT! Gently though, GENTLY! Last time you pulled something in a library we got banned from Brixton Public for LIFE! And keep one eye on that Sneekly character, Clyde — he's been fiddling with that mantelpiece like a man who knows more than he's letting on! Right, here goes nothing — Dum-Dum, pull that upside-down book! FOR CLARA!

I've got this terrible feeling in me gut, and it ain't from the dodgy kebab I had on the way here. Them upside-down books are OBVIOUSLY part of some mechanism — even WE can see that, and we can barely see past our own noses most days. But here's what's really eating at me: Sneekly got to that mantelpiece FIRST. He 'interacted' with it before anyone else could have a proper look. What if he's DISABLED something? What if the secret passage was supposed to lead to Clara and he's gone and blocked it off? I can't prove nothing — me brain don't work that way — but me INSTINCTS are screaming louder than Dum-Dum when he sits on a drawing pin. We pull this book, something happens, and we stumble our way closer to Clara. That's how it works with us — we ain't clever, but we're ACCIDENTALLY brilliant!

Penelope Pitstop: Well, butter my biscuits! I do believe somethin' shifted when I pressed that stone! Did y'all hear that little *click*? Oh, my heart is just RACIN'! There's nothin' more exhilaratin' than a genuine hidden mechanism in a genuine old manor house! Let me get a closer look at what we've uncovered here — a lady's keen eye misses nothin', especially when there's a legendary Diamond at stake! Peter, darlin', you were examinin' this too — did you see where that panel moved?

Every instinct I have is screamin' that this mantelpiece is the first real breadcrumb on the trail to the Doily Diamond. If there's a map hidden inside, it could show the whole layout of Lord Bellingham's puzzle trail. And I notice Dick Dastardly is awfully interested in those upside-down books — could they be part of the same mechanism? Oh, Clara, you clever thing, you're onto somethin' BIG!
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, dear me — just as I feared! Several of these volumes have been placed UPSIDE DOWN, which is a telltale sign of moisture warping, you see. The spines curl and one replaces them incorrectly in haste. Allow me to just... correct these... one must handle antique bindings with the UTMOST care...

The Ant Hill Mob grows SUSPICIOUS — curse their beady little eyes! 'What candles?' they ask. WHAT CANDLES INDEED! A minor oversight in my otherwise FLAWLESS performance. But no matter — while they watch Penelope paw at the mantelpiece like a kitten with a ball of yarn, Vincent Marsh shall unlock the TRUE secret of this library! These upside-down books are CLEARLY a combination — a sequence to be pulled in the correct order! Lord Bellingham was a CARTOGRAPHER, the riddle speaks of a MAP, and maps require KEYS and LEGENDS! Oh, the magnificent symmetry of it all! Pull the right books in the right order, and the treasure map reveals itself to the one person in this room with the VISION to claim it! And if anyone asks why the estate manager is rearranging books during a treasure hunt... well, water damage waits for NO man! Mwa-ha-ha-HA!

Dick Dastardly: Ah, Rufus! Sawtooth! How DELIGHTFUL to find you both here! I was just coming to warn you — this laboratory is EXTREMELY dangerous! Full of volatile chemicals and unstable machinery! You should probably leave IMMEDIATELY! In fact, I insist! But first — what are these dusty old crates? Probably nothing important, just old junk. Nobody look at them! Especially not ME!

Heh heh HEH! Tell them to leave, and they'll stay out of sheer stubbornness! Meanwhile, the GREAT Reginald Foxworth will investigate these crates for hidden treasures! And that machine — THREE operators, you say? Well, if I MUST use these two buffoons to operate it, I suppose I'll graciously allow them to pull levers while I position myself at the OUTPUT end to catch whatever pops out! I am a GENIUS of unparalleled magnitude!
Dick Dastardly examined the crates.

The Ant Hill Mob: Well THAT was a fat lot of nothing! The books won't budge — probably GLUED in, the rotten things! Right, never mind the shelves, lads — look at the MANTELPIECE! Miss Pitstop and Peter both heard something CLICK! There's a mechanism in there, plain as day! Dum-Dum, give me a boost so I can get a proper look at that stonework — NO, not like that, you'll — OI! DUM-DUM, YOUR FOOT'S ON MY — AAARGH!

Right, so the bookshelves are a dead end. Literally. Won't interact, won't budge, won't do NOTHING. But the mantelpiece — that's where it's at. Peter felt something shift, Penelope heard a click. If we can just get our clumsy mitts on it, something'll happen. It always does with us — we fall face-first into success. And I'm keeping me beady eye on Sneekly the whole time. He was fiddling with that mantelpiece earlier, and I'd bet me last penny he was trying to STOP it from opening, not help it along. If there's a hidden passage to Clara behind that stonework, we're going through it — headfirst and probably upside down, but we're going THROUGH it!
The Ant Hill Mob interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, it's a MAP! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — that's a MAP, plain as peaches in July! And Mr. Pemberton, you sweet man, you practically GAVE us the answer when you mentioned Lord Bellingham was a cartographer! Now Peter, darlin', you said you felt a mechanism shift — well I heard a little *click* myself just now! I do believe this mantelpiece is ready to give up its secret! Let me try speakin' the answer right to it — sometimes these old puzzle-boxes are just WAITIN' for someone with the proper refinement to say the magic word! A MAP! Show us what you're hidin', you gorgeous old stonework!

Oh, I am just TINGLING with excitement! A hidden map in a cartographer's mantelpiece — this HAS to lead to the Doily Diamond! And isn't everyone just the NICEST? That dear Mr. Pemberton helping us along, Dick Dastardly bravely checking the dangerous laboratory so we don't have to — I am surrounded by ANGELS!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Ha HA! Did you all feel that? The stonework SHIFTED! I KNEW it — precision engineering instincts, never wrong! Now let me get a proper look at what we've uncovered here. A map, perhaps? A secret compartment? Lord Bellingham was a cartographer, after all — and a man who carves riddles into his mantelpiece doesn't do it for idle decoration! This is it, everyone — this is the BREAKTHROUGH! And when Clara hears that James Hartwell cracked the Library's first secret... well, let's just say some discoveries are worth more than diamonds!

Please let there be something spectacular behind this panel. A map, a key, ANYTHING. If it's just a loose brick I will simply perish of embarrassment right here in front of Penelope and the Mob and that suspicious estate manager. No — THINK POSITIVE, James. Fortune favours the bold, and the bold favour Clara Bellingham!
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah — dear me, dear ME! Miss Pitstop, Mr. Hartwell, I must insist you step back from the mantelpiece at once! I heard that click as well, and as estate manager I am DUTY-BOUND to inspect any activated mechanisms before guests proceed! Lord Bellingham was known for his... protective measures, shall we say. Booby traps for the unwary! Allow me to examine this properly — I am intimately familiar with the manor's architectural quirks. The answer to the inscription, of course, is quite elementary for anyone who knew Lord Bellingham — a MAP! He was a cartographer, after all! Now let me just... apply the correct pressure to the right stone...

YES! The answer is MAP — a cartographer's riddle hiding a cartographer's treasure! While these fools fumble and paw at the stonework like children pressing elevator buttons, VINCENT MARSH shall solve the puzzle with the precision of a master criminal! And if the mechanism reveals something dangerous — a trapdoor, a gas release, a swinging blade — well, what a TRAGIC accident it would be if dear Clara happened to be standing in the wrong spot! Every trap in this manor is a TOOL for the magnificently wicked! Mwa-ha-ha!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, would you LOOK at that! The stonework shifted just like a charm — Lord Bellingham must have been just the cleverest man! Now let me get a good look at what's been hidin' in there all these years.
